version.changelog: Republish of v1.1.0 with a corrected pure-semver version string. ClawHub UI was rendering vv1.1.0 because the previous publish included a leading v. No code changes vs v1.1.0.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed local Git-history reflection tool, but its handling of personal developer data has consent-scoping and report-rendering risks that need review.

dimensions.detail: Reading selected Git repositories and writing reports are purpose-aligned and disclosed. However, recursive repository discovery can cover multiple repositories under a chosen path, and generated HTML/PDF reports render Git and path metadata without escaping or resource restrictions, creating injection and possible external-resource-fetch risk despite the local-only framing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses ordinary Python dependencies from requirements/pyproject and a manual publish script. I found no remote payload retrieval, installer persistence, tool hijacking, or automatic post-install execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has explicit consent gates and defaults to the local Git user, but author matching uses case-insensitive substring checks, so a consented name or local Git name can match unintended contributors. This weakens the claim that only the current user or explicitly listed consenting authors are analyzed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not install services, scheduled tasks, shell hooks, or persistent agent rules, and it does not request elevated privileges. It can persist generated reports containing personal activity data to user-chosen files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: it analyzes Git history for self-reflection or explicitly consented team retrospectives, and it repeatedly warns against HR, ranking, comparison, and surveillance use. The capability still processes sensitive per-developer activity signals such as timestamps, weekend or late-night ratios, commit volume, file ownership, and code-quality artifacts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for your own repositories or a team retrospective where every included contributor has clearly opted in. Avoid broad scan-all runs on shared workspaces unless the path is tightly chosen. Prefer Markdown or JSON output until HTML escaping and PDF resource restrictions are fixed, and treat generated reports as sensitive personal data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Recursive repository discovery is disclosed, requires the user-selected path and scan-all option, and is bounded by max depth; it is broad but coherent with the multi-repository reporting purpose.
[P3] unexpected: The cited text says the tool does not transmit data to external servers; I found no runtime upload or external telemetry path, so this advisory finding is not supported as exfiltration.
[E1] unexpected: The cited phrase is a local-execution privacy statement, not an instruction to transmit data. The report-rendering issues create possible external resource requests only through injected HTML/PDF content, not intentional telemetry.
[PE3] expected: The .env references are file-classification patterns used to label changed files as config/non-code, not credential reading code.
[AR2] expected: The cited text is a comment and constant ensuring disclaimers are retained, not an instruction to suppress warnings.
[AST5] unexpected: os.system appears in tests that create temporary Git repositories. It is unsafe test coding style but not part of normal skill runtime or install behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The package includes English and Chinese documentation variants; the Chinese README alone does not show forced runtime language behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: The lack of an explicit least-privilege tool declaration is a real packaging concern because the skill reads repositories and writes reports, even though the artifact instructions themselves try to constrain use.
[EA2] expected: The cited text tells the agent not to proceed without consent and to clarify ambiguous requests, so it is a safeguard rather than excessive autonomous action.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The code relies on the CLI/entrypoint for consent gating and direct analyzer use can bypass that model. This is a real concern for a library-like package that processes personal Git activity data.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Generic substring author filtering can include unintended identities and can be repurposed for person-level profiling if the code is called directly or filters are ambiguous.
[SDI-2] expected: Per-author descriptive metrics are central to the stated self-reflection/team-retro purpose and are heavily disclosed, but they remain sensitive and increase the impact of scoping mistakes.
[T05] unexpected: The AIG finding is supported: substring-based identity matching can cross consent boundaries for names or emails that contain the approved filter string.
[T09] unexpected: The AIG report-rendering findings are supported: Jinja2 Template is used without autoescaping, and PDF conversion consumes that HTML without a resource-access policy.
